newsitem.title: USA: Jury views Jenny Jones show at heart of murder.
newsitem.headline: Jury views Jenny Jones show at heart of murder.

text.p: Jurors in Jonathan Schmitz's murder trial showed little emotion Thursday as they watched a never-before played segment of the "Jenny Jones" talk show on secret admirers and their same-sex crushes.

Schmitz, 26, of Lake Orion, a northern suburb of Detroit, is charged with first-degree murder in the death of Scott Amedure, 32, of Orion Township, in Oakland County Circuit Court. The two had appeared with a mutual female friend, Donna Riley, on the segment taped March 6, 1995, three days before Amedure was killed.

Schmitz, who says he is straight, has said the humiliation of the show, combined with various mental illnesses he suffers from, contributed to his killing Amedure with two shotgun blasts to the chest.
Host Jenny Jones, to the loud cheering of the studio audience, tells the camera that her guests have chosen to tell their secret admirers they are gay on national television.
"First of all, it takes a lot guts to do this -- a lot of guts," Jones says.
She goes on to say the show has flown six men and women to Chicago who know someone has a crush on them, but that is all.
While Schmitz is kept back stage unaware of what is being said, Amedure recounts his fantasies for Schmitz, and Riley tells how she has tried to play matchmaker between the two.
Asked by Jones if Schmitz is gay, Riley responds, "He's a very open person, so it really woudn't surprise me."

When Schmitz is brought out and told that it is Amedure who has the crush, he laughs and says, "You lied to me." Schmitz appears surprised but not distraught on the tape, although he covered his face with embarrassment when the tape of Amedure's fantasy is replayed.
"I'm definitely a heterosexual," Schmitz says on the tape.
Prosecutor Roman Kalytiak described the jury as "businesslike" as they watched the tape. But defence attorney James Burdick said he believed it made a strong impression on them.
"I think they were surprised to see how truly venal the show was," he said.

Under questioning from Kalytiak, Riley said Amedure was never aggressive toward Schmitz or tried to pressure him sexually. She said Schmitz and Amedure had talked previously at her apartment about Amedure's homosexuality and whether Amedure's parents knew was gay.
"They were joking about it. Jonathan was asking a lot of questions," she said, adding he seemed "very" inquisitive about the topic.
Riley also said Schmitz had asked if Amedure would be able to help Schmitz select and install ceiling fans in his dining room and bedroom on Sunday, March 12.
The testimony could be important, because Schmitz' father as well as his lawyers have said Amedure stalked Schmitz despite attempts to stop his advances.

The jury will have the option of convicting Schmitz of first- or second-degree murder, manslaughter, or reckless discharge causing death. The first-degree murder charge carries a penalty of life without possibility of parole.
